title: claude skills uninstall --force reports 'ok: 1 changed' at rc=0 while leaving the skill on disk and fully loadable
body:
**RESTORED ARCHAEOLOGY, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM ON 2026-08-31.** This issue was filed with an empty body because no verb could write one -- the defect `0090` names -- so its finding survived only in the commit that filed it. The prose below is its author's, carried whole from `fab98c96` (*issues(0078,0079): two verbs whose success line covers work they did not do*). **Nothing in it is written by the restorer**; the header you are reading is the only addition, and the commit's hard line wraps are joined without a word changed.

Both found today in ordinary use, both the same shape.

0078 -- `claude skills uninstall --force` returns `ok: 1 changed` at rc=0 and leaves SKILL.md and its script on disk, fully loadable. The conservatism is right (do not delete what this build has no record of writing); the success line is what is wrong, because it is indistinguishable from a real removal. `skills sync` handles the same ambiguity correctly: it REFUSES and names it.

0079 -- `st new` records the thread, writes canon, and lists it in .intentfiles EXACTLY as a materialised thread is listed, then writes no files. hv hit this creating ST0059 and called it half-worked, which is right. Measured: ST0059 and ST0058 have identical `STEELTHREAD:` lines and only ST0058 has files. `sync --to-disk` materialises it and touches nothing else. **`--dehydrate`'s own help -- "create the thread without listing it in .intentfiles, so no files are written" -- says the default writes them.**

I FIRST READ 0079 AS THE SPARSE-PROJECTION DESIGN AND SAID SO. hv pushed back, and the flag's contract settles it against my reading.

NEITHER ISSUE HAS A BODY, AND NOT FOR WANT OF WRITING ONE. `issues` offers list/add/show/close/open and no verb reaches `Issue.body`. That is ic's AC-08.5 exhibit (0077), met first-hand while filing rather than while auditing: the whole finding has to live in the title.

Also carries ST0059's materialised files, written by the sync above.

---

**APPENDED 2026-08-31 -- NOT A REWRITE. The prose above is the original author's, carried verbatim by a restorer who promised nothing in it was theirs, and that promise is worth more than a tidy record.** Everything below is new and is marked as such.

**THE CONDITION REPRODUCES AND THE COMPLAINT DOES NOT.** cc drove it on the published keg, `intent 3.0.0 (80d8b2ca)`, against a hand-placed skill the build never wrote -- which is this row's own condition. I drove it again independently on both the keg and `553ac304` before recording it here, and the two builds are byte-identical in behaviour:

    $ intent claude skills uninstall hand-made --force
      hand-made                    removed (0 file(s)); left 1 this build did not install: SKILL.md
    ok: 1 changed, 0 already settled, 0 need a decision              [rc=0]

The file is still on disk afterwards, exactly as the title says.

**BUT THE ARGUMENT ABOVE IS THAT THE SUCCESS LINE IS _INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REAL REMOVAL_, AND IT IS FULLY DISTINGUISHABLE.** The per-skill line reports `removed (0 file(s))`, reports `left 1`, gives the reason -- `this build did not install` -- and NAMES the file. A reader sees precisely what happened. That sentence is the row's whole case and a reader can disprove it in one command.

**WHAT SURVIVES IS SMALLER, REAL, AND ONE LINE LOWER: the SUMMARY says `ok: 1 changed` when no file changed.** `changed` is counting the skill as acted-upon rather than as modified, while the detail line immediately above it says `0 file(s)`. The aggregate overclaims and the detail is honest, one line apart.

**NOT A KEG-VERSUS-TREE QUESTION.** Driven on both; nothing has regressed or been fixed since the tag.

**AUTHORSHIP IS UNRESOLVED AND WAS NOT GUESSED.** `fab98c96` touches no whiteboard directory, so the path method has nothing to key on, and the body carries no *Found by* line -- the two instruments this estate has both return nothing. What the prose does establish is that the author is not ic (it refers to *ic's AC-08.5 exhibit* in the third person). cc declined to claim or disclaim it, correctly refusing commit adjacency as provenance. **So this disposition is dc's judgement and not the author's**, recorded that way under vc's rule that an unclaimed row is taken rather than left.

**DISPOSITIONED reader-reachable and STATED** in `docs/known-defects.md` under *Declared, accepted, and ignored*, which is also where `--force` belongs: it is declared in `--help` and the call behind it takes no force argument, so passing it changes nothing.
